items.title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Society of Cardiovascular Surgery/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Clinical Practice Update on Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Valve Intervention: Patient Evaluation and Management.
items.abstract: The management of mitral valve (MV) and tricuspid valve (TV) regurgitation has undergone significant transformation during the past decade. This change has been driven by a growing understanding of the adverse clinical consequences of these conditions, particularly their strong association with heart failure progression, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality-and by the emergence of effective transcatheter options for valve intervention. Among these, transcatheter MV edge-to-edge repair and replacement and transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair and replacement have become important therapeutic tools that provide a less invasive alternative to surgery in appropriately selected patients. In this clinical practice update we aim to provide contemporary, evidence-based guidance for clinicians in the evaluation and management of patients with severe, symptomatic MV or TV regurgitation who might benefit from transcatheter intervention. Key topics include the clinical presentation of these valve lesions, the diagnostic evaluation with emphasis on multimodality imaging and hemodynamics, criteria for patient selection, and current data on procedural and long-term clinical outcomes. A central theme is the role of timely referral and structured assessment to avoid missed opportunities for intervention. Optimal outcomes require active engagement from referring physicians and close collaboration within a multidisciplinary heart team, including cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, imaging specialists, heart failure specialists, and nursing partners-to ensure careful patient selection, procedural planning, and comprehensive post-intervention follow-up. By integrating clinical judgement with guideline-based recommendations and procedural expertise, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair or transcatheter valve replacement can offer substantial symptomatic relief and improved quality of life for selected patients, while minimizing procedural risk and enhancing overall cardiovascular outcomes.

QT Interval Prolongation in Athletes With Negative Genetic Testing and Complete Normalization After Detraining.
items.abstract: QT interval prolongation is traditionally associated with congenital or acquired long QT syndrome; however, its interpretation in athletes remains challenging because of possible exercise-induced electrophysiological adaptations. We report a case series of 4 competitive athletes referred to our Sports Cardiology clinic after incidental detection of marked QT interval prolongation during preparticipation screening for sports eligibility. All individuals were asymptomatic, took no QT interval-prolonging drugs, had normal electrolyte levels, and had negative family screening and genetic testing. Following a detraining period of 3-6 months, repeat electrocardiograms showed consistent normalization of both QT interval and corrected QT intervals in all cases. The magnitude of the corrected QT interval reduction was substantial and observed intraindividually, independently of significant changes in heart rate. These findings support the concept that, in some athletes, QT interval prolongation may represent a dynamic and reversible phenotype related to training load, termed "exercise-induced" long QT interval. Recognition of this pattern may help avoid misdiagnosis of congenital long QT syndrome and inappropriate restriction from competitive sports, although its long-term arrhythmic risk remains unclear.

items.title: Renal Cell Carcinoma Isolated to the Left Ventricle 10 Years After Initial Resection.
items.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) accounts for 3% of solid malignancies, with clear cell RCC (ccRCC) comprising 80% of cases. Although 20%-30% of RCC cases are metastatic at diagnosis, cardiac metastases are rare. A 65-year-old man with a remote history of ccRCC developed progressive dyspnea. Evaluation showed pulmonary nodules and a fluorodeoxyglucose-avid left ventricular mass. Surgical resection confirmed ccRCC. He received dual immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and achieved a complete response. His treatment was complicated by pneumonitis, which resolved with corticosteroids. He remains in remission off therapy. This is a rare case of oligorecurrent RCC with cardiac metastasis without inferior vena cava involvement after prolonged remission. It emphasizes the complexity of decision-making because of extracardiac metastasis and treatment complications. Cardiac metastasis is rare in oligorecurrent RCC, but relapse may occur even after prolonged latency periods. Appropriate treatment requires identification of other metastatic sites and a multidisciplinary approach.

items.title: Labetalol-induced hyperkalemia in acute aortic dissection: A rare but clinically relevant adverse effect.
items.abstract: Hyperkalemia is a potentially life-threatening electrolyte abnormality often associated with renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibitors, renal dysfunction, or potassium-sparing agents. Non-selective beta-blockers, including labetalol, may also precipitate hyperkalemia through beta-2 (β-2)-adrenergic blockade, although this adverse effect is underrecognized, particularly in patients without underlying renal disease. A 59-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes, asthma, and polysubstance use disorder presented with severe chest pain and hypertensive emergency (243/132 mmHg). Imaging revealed aortic dilatation and confirmed acute type B aortic dissection. After initial medical management with intravenous (IV) esmolol and nicardipine, oral labetalol was initiated and escalated to 600 mg for anti-impulse therapy. The patient developed persistent, non-hemolyzed hyperkalemia (5.2 to 5.8 mmol/L) temporally correlating with labetalol dose escalation, despite preserved renal function (serum creatinine 1.4 to 1.8 mg/dL) and absence of RAAS inhibitors or heparin exposure. Conservative management failed, and the patient underwent thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) with thoracic branch endoprosthesis (TBE). Post-operatively, labetalol was discontinued and replaced with carvedilol. Serum potassium (K+) normalized within 48 hours and remained without further K+ lowering agents. Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale assessment yielded a score of 7, indicating a probable adverse drug reaction. Labetalol may induce clinically significant hyperkalemia independent of renal impairment or typical precipitating medications. This case highlights the importance of monitoring K+ in patients receiving labetalol for acute aortic syndromes and supports carvedilol as a potentially safer non-selective beta-blocker alternative with respect to K+ homeostasis.

items.title: Launching an independent research laboratory and scientific career: Tools for a rapidly changing landscape.
items.abstract: Scientific independence alone does not create a sustainable research program. Drawing on the 2026 Irving Cancer Immunology Symposium, we offer practical strategies for navigating uncertainty and limited resources to build a coherent research program and resilient team across funding systems.

items.title: Supplementation with Akkermansia muciniphila Enhances the αPD-1 Efficacy in Mice Transplanted with Gut Microbiota from Patients with Colorectal Cancer.
items.abstract: The resistance of colorectal cancer (CRC) to PD-1 blockade has positioned it as a critical focus of global research efforts. The gut microbiota is a key regulator of anti-tumor immunity, but research on bacteria that are clearly associated with primary resistance to PD-1 blockade in colorectal cancer remains incomplete. In this study, C57BL/6 mice were subjected to antibiotic pretreatment to deplete endogenous gut microbiota. The mice were then gavaged with fecal suspensions from treatment-naïve CRC patients or healthy donors, subsequently implanted with MC38 tumor cells to establish the tumor model, and then treated with the drug. Gut microbial composition was analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing, while tumor-infiltrating immune cells and cytokine profiles were characterized using flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry, respectively. CRC patient microbiota conferred resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in mice, an effect completely reversed by oral Akkermansia muciniphila (Akk). Mechanistically, Akk reconfigured the tumor immune microenvironment, leading to a substantial increase in CD8+ T cell infiltration and function. Crucially, this potent local anti-tumor immunity was achieved without systemic immune activation. In summary, this study establishes that Akk amplifies the local CD8⁺ T cell response, sensitizing tumors to anti-PD-1 therapy, without inducing a systemic inflammatory response. These findings position Akk supplementation as a promising, targeted strategy to overcome PD-1 immunotherapy resistance of MSS-CRC with a favorable safety profile.

items.title: Alveolar macrophage heterogeneity in pulmonary hypertension: pathogenic mechanisms and precision intervention.
items.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) involves complex interactions between immune dysfunction and pulmonary vascular remodeling. Alveolar macrophages (AMs) are important regulators linking pulmonary immune responses to vascular pathology. However, AMs are not a homogeneous population and undergo dynamic functional reprogramming in response to chronic hypoxia, endothelial injury, metabolic stress, and extracellular matrix remodeling. This review summarizes current evidence on the mechanisms and pathological roles of AM heterogeneity in PH, focusing on cellular origin, microenvironmental regulation, transcriptional control, metabolic reprogramming, and intercellular crosstalk. We further discuss how distinct AM functional states contribute to chronic inflammation, pulmonary vascular remodeling, and disease progression. Importantly, we highlight AM state-specific regulation as a potential therapeutic strategy. Understanding AM heterogeneity as a dynamic process of functional adaptation may provide a new framework for elucidating immune mechanisms in PH and developing more precise therapeutic approaches.

items.title: [Metastatic or recurrent cervical cancer : current management and therapeutic perspectives].
items.abstract: Cervical cancer is the fourth most common cancer in women. Despite advances in screening and vaccination against human papillomavirus (HPV), some patients are still initially diagnosed at a metastatic stage, while others subsequently develop a disseminated disease, associated with a particularly poor prognosis. Until recently, first-line treatment was only based on platinum-based chemotherapy combined, in the absence of contraindications, with bevacizumab, a monoclonal antibody that inhibits angiogenesis. However, this approach has recently evolved with the introduction of immunotherapy and the development of other innovative therapies currently under study, offering hope for improving survival in these patients. Le cancer du col de l’utérus est le quatrième cancer le plus fréquent chez la femme. En dépit des progrès du dépistage et de la vaccination contre le papillomavirus humain (HPV), certaines patientes sont encore diagnostiquées à un stade d’emblée métastatique de la maladie, tandis que d’autres développent secondairement une forme disséminée, associée à un pronostic particulièrement défavorable. Le traitement de première ligne reposait, jusqu’à récemment, essentiellement sur une chimiothérapie à base de sels de platine, associée, en l’absence de contre-indication, au bévacizumab, un anticorps monoclonal inhibant l’angiogenèse. Cependant, cette prise en charge a évolué ces dernières années avec l’introduction de l’immunothérapie et le développement d’autres thérapies innovantes en cours d’étude, offrant la perspective d’améliorer la survie de ces patientes.

items.title: Machine learning-driven SERS fingerprinting for high-accuracy serum screening of hepatic inflammation in mice.
items.abstract: Hepatitis screening is clinically challenging. Conventional serological and biochemical assays rely on cumbersome procedures, require long detection times, and lack sufficient sensitivity to identify pathological changes. Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) enables rapid, label-free, and high-sensitivity molecular fingerprinting of biological fluids. It holds great promise for noninvasive serum biochemical analysis. Here, we report a machine learning-enhanced SERS platform based on a sugar-cube-like Ag nanocrystal (SC-AgN) substrate for accurate discrimination between healthy and DMN-induced hepatitis mouse serum. We fabricated the SC-AgN substrate with favourable uniformity, reproducibility and SERS enhancement to capture robust and well-resolved spectra from mouse serum samples. Clear spectral differences were identified in hepatitis serum, which correspond to protein denaturation, lipid peroxidation, and disturbed nucleic acid metabolism. Principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to reduce dimensionality, remove spectral noise, and eliminate redundant spectral features. The optimized spectral variables were further imported into a sparse partial least-squares discriminant analysis (SPLS-DA) model for precise sample classification. The finalized PCA-SPLS-DA model achieved an accuracy of 96.7%, a sensitivity of 100.0%, a specificity of 94.6%, and an AUC of 0.973 (95% CI, 0.945-0.992) for distinguishing DMN-induced hepatitis from healthy serum samples. This diagnostic performance outperforms that of conventional spectroscopic approaches. This work establishes a robust SC-AgN-based SERS diagnostic strategy integrated with the PCA-SPLS-DA model, which is expected to provide a rapid, low-cost and high-accuracy solution for hepatitis screening and auxiliary clinical diagnosis.

items.title: Temporal dissection of hepatitis C virus and orthoflavivirus infections by continuous luminescence monitoring.
items.abstract: Virus infection is a dynamic process consisting of rapidly evolving viral and host events, yet conventional endpoint assays provide only fragmented snapshots of these processes. Here, we established a unified temporal framework for dissecting virus-host interactions by integrating continuous bioluminescence monitoring with molecular and functional analyses. Real-time monitoring of hepatitis C virus (HCV) single-round infectious particles (SRIPs) revealed a biphasic replication profile consisting of an initial transient phase, followed by replication-dependent amplification. This transition was independently validated by similar HCV RNA kinetics observed after infection with HCV SRIPs or fully infectious HCV. Extension of this approach to dengue, Zika, and yellow fever virus SRIPs demonstrated that infection kinetics are determined by virus-specific replication programs and are modulated by the combination of viral replicons/capsids and prM/E proteins. This temporal framework enabled the identification of virus-host interactions that are difficult to resolve by conventional endpoint analyses. Early-phase cytoplasmic proteomics, combined with functional screening, identified the dynein light chain component DYNLRB2 as a previously unrecognized negative regulator of early HCV infection. Continuous monitoring also distinguished phase-specific antiviral activities, revealing distinct kinetic inhibition profiles for daclatasvir, acetylsalicylic acid, and interferon-α. Furthermore, delayed activation of the ER stress sensor ATF6 was first detected 40-47 h after HCV infection, and transcriptomic analysis at reporter-defined time points characterized the accompanying transition in host gene expression. Together, our study establishes continuous temporal monitoring as a general strategy for resolving dynamic virus-host interactions and for uncovering molecular events that remain obscured by conventional endpoint analyses.IMPORTANCEViral infection is a dynamic process in which entry, genome amplification, host-factor requirements, antiviral effects, and cellular responses occur on different timescales. Conventional endpoint assays can identify changes in these processes but provide limited information about when they emerge or transition from one stage to another. Here, we show that continuous monitoring, when combined with direct molecular and functional measurements, can place these otherwise separate observations within a common temporal framework. Using HCV and related orthoflavivirus SRIPs, we resolved early and replication-associated phases, identified host factors with stage-dependent effects, and distinguished profiles of antiviral inhibition. We further showed that ATF6-mediated ER stress activation emerged later than early HCV infection and viral RNA amplification. Thus, continuous temporal monitoring provides a general strategy for resolving dynamic virus-host interactions by defining the temporal relationships among viral processes, pharmacological effects, and host responses that remain obscured by conventional endpoint analyses.

items.title: Vaccination for girls and women across the life course: Evidence-based recommendations for clinical practice and policy.
items.abstract: Vaccination across the life course is a cornerstone of preventive health care for girls and women. Although WHO recommends completion of essential vaccines by adolescence, global coverage remains suboptimal. Vaccine-preventable diseases-including HPV-related cancers, vaginal, vulvar, anal, oropharyngeal, influenza, pertussis, hepatitis B, herpes zoster, and pneumococcal disease-continue to impose a disproportionate burden on girls and women, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and migrant populations. Key life stages, such as childhood (early and middle), adolescence, preconception, pregnancy, postpartum, midlife, and beyond, offer critical opportunities for immunization. Obstetricians, gynecologists, midwives, and other women's healthcare providers are uniquely positioned to integrate vaccination into routine care in all settings and influence vaccine acceptance. Strengthening vaccine advocacy within women's health care is essential to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality and advance health equity for girls and women globally. This paper presents evidence-based recommendations for equitable vaccination across the life course of girls and women, synthesizing guidance from WHO, the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and national immunization technical advisory groups. Vaccines reviewed include HPV, tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis (Tdap), influenza, hepatitis B, measles-mumps-rubella (MMR), varicella, herpes zoster, pneumococcal, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and COVID-19. A life-course framework is proposed, emphasizing maternal immunization, cervical cancer prevention, and integration of regular and opportune vaccination into routine obstetric and gynecologic services. Practical implementation strategies and policy recommendations are outlined to support FIGO member societies.

items.title: GPR82-mediated activation of TGF-β/SMAD signaling contributes to CD8 + T cell dysfunction in HBV-ACLF.
items.abstract: Patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) have severe CD8 + T cell dysfunction. This study examined G protein-coupled receptor 82 (GPR82) in CD8 + T cell exhaustion in hepatitis B virus-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF). Using GEO analysis, clinical samples, GPR82 manipulation, transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β)/SMAD intervention, dual-luciferase assays, and a mouse hepatitis virus strain 3 (MHV-3) mouse model, we found GPR82 overexpression in ACLF liver and HBV-ACLF CD8 + T cells, correlating with T cell exhaustion. GPR82 knockdown enhanced CD8 + T cell function, while overexpression had opposite effects. Mechanistically, lysophosphatidylcholine (LysoPC) upregulated GPR82 transcription via TGF-β/SMAD1, and elevated GPR82 further activated TGF-β/SMAD, forming a positive feedback loop. In vivo , GPR82 knockdown partially restored CD8 + T cell function and alleviated liver injury in the MHV-3 mouse model. These findings indicate GPR82 promotes CD8 + T cell exhaustion via TGF-β/SMAD, and the LysoPC-GPR82 loop offers insight into ACLF immune dysfunction, suggesting GPR82 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target.

items.title: Presumed hepatic pseudolipoma detected as a small hepatic surface lesion: multimodality imaging findings.
items.abstract: Hepatic pseudolipomas are uncommon benign lesions located on or near the liver capsule which are thought to arise from a detached epiploic appendage that becomes trapped near Glisson's capsule. Because these lesions may appear as small hepatic or perihepatic nodules, they can mimic primary or metastatic hepatic tumors on screening imaging. Here, we report the case of a 55-year-old asymptomatic man with no relevant medical history who was referred after routine health-screening ultrasonography revealed a 10 × 8-mm hyperechoic lesion adjacent to the surface of liver segment VI. Liver function tests were normal, hepatitis B and C viral markers were negative, and tumor markers, including carcinoembryonic antigen, carbohydrate antigen 19-9, alpha-fetoprotein, and protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist-II, were within the normal ranges. Dynamic ultrasonography demonstrated that the lesion was located along the hepatic capsule, rather than within the deep hepatic parenchyma. Computed tomography showed a well-demarcated hepatic surface lesion with central calcification and surrounding fat attenuation, without any arterial, portal venous, or delayed enhancement. Gadoxetate disodium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging revealed fat-containing signal characteristics, no hepatobiliary-phase uptake, and no diffusion restriction. The integrated multimodal imaging findings supported a diagnosis of presumed hepatic pseudolipoma, likely originating from a detached epiploic appendage. Recognition of this benign hepatic tumor mimic may help to avoid unnecessary biopsy or surgery.

items.title: Quantifying the Role of Interventional Radiology in Managing Patients with Hepatobiliary Cancers.
items.abstract: To quantify the role of interventional radiology (IR) in managing primary and secondary hepatobiliary cancers. This retrospective study analyzed administrative data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) using final action claims for Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries from 2016 to 2021. Patients aged ≥65 years with hepatobiliary cancer were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD), 10th Revision, codes. Services and associated work Relative Value Units (wRVUs) provided by IR, medical oncology, radiation oncology, and surgical oncology were identified using CMS physician specialty codes. IR procedures were classified as therapeutic or supportive. From 2016 to 2021, the Medicare hepatobiliary cancer cohort included 108,317-111,761 patients annually (mean age, 75 years; male, 53%). Medical oncologists treated 70% of patients, followed by interventional radiologists with 51%, radiation oncologists with 13%, and surgical oncologists with 5%. Physician service volumes and wRVU remained stable, with medical oncologists providing the largest share (69% of services and 13.7% of wRVUs), followed by interventional radiologists (2.9% and 11.7%, respectively), radiation oncologists (1.3% and 4.5%, respectively), and surgical oncologists (0.1% and 2.2%, respectively). Interventional radiologists performed 75,785 therapeutic procedures, primarily for hepatocellular carcinoma (59%). Before pandemic, IR volumes increased 57%, driven by liver ablations (+25%) and supportive services (+63%), whereas transarterial therapies declined slightly (-6%). Despite the drop in volume during the pandemic, IR saw the highest compound annual growth rate (4%) among the specialties analyzed. IR provides a substantial share of services for patients with hepatobiliary cancers, with rising use of therapeutic and supportive services, delivering similar wRVUs at lower costs, underscoring its growing role in cancer care.

items.title: Successful Use of Sutimlimab in two Pediatric Patients With Refractory Cold Antibody-Mediated Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia.
items.abstract: Cold antibody-mediated autoimmune hemolytic anemia, or cold agglutinin syndrome (CAS), in pediatrics is typically transient, although it can often be severe and require transfusion support. Recurrence in children is rare, but those with underlying immune dysfunction can have a refractory course with limited options available. We report a 4-year-old girl with Evans syndrome and life-threatening CAS refractory to transfusions, plasmapheresis, steroids, and immunosuppression as well as a 12-month-old boy status post liver transplant with CAS refractory to steroids, rituximab, and tacrolimus cessation with transition to sirolimus, both of whom received sutimlimab, a C1s inhibitor, with rapid improvement in hemolysis, transfusion independence, and a sustained remission. To our knowledge, these are the first reported uses of sutimlimab in the pediatric population.

items.title: Survival and mortality in adults with cancer and pre-existing mental illness across multimorbidity types: a decade of population-based data from Alberta, Canada.
items.abstract: Adults living with cancer and pre-existing mental illness (PMI) represent a particularly vulnerable population. This study examined whether multimorbidity protects against or increases mortality among adults with cancer and PMI. We used Alberta Health Services administrative data ( n  = 15,144), to identify adults with both PMI and cancer diagnosed between 2013-2022, including demographic, comorbidity, and cancer information. The analysis used Cox proportional hazard models (HR) to evaluate the impact among different multimorbidity categories on all-cause mortality. The multimorbidity categories were classified as cardiometabolic (e.g. cardiovascular disease), musculoskeletal (e.g. rheumatic disease), chronic airway (e.g. chronic pulmonary disease), and general multimorbidity (e.g. including liver and renal disease). Multimorbidity combinations were defined as the presence of conditions across two or more categories. In a cohort of 15,144 adults with cancer, 39.1% died during follow-up. In the overall cohort, compared with those without multimorbidity, adjusted models showed that multimorbidity increased mortality for cardiometabolic conditions (HR = 1.25, 95%CI 1.13-1.37), chronic airway disease (HR = 1.88, 95%CI 1.69-2.08), general multimorbidity (HR = 1.90, 95%CI 1.59-2.27), and multimorbidity combinations (HR = 2.29, 95%CI 2.08-2.51). Musculoskeletal conditions were not significant. By PMI subtype, multimorbidity combinations were consistently associated with increased mortality across mood, anxiety, substance use, and multiple psychiatric disorders (HRs = 1.67-1.91). General multimorbidity was associated with increased mortality in anxiety, substance use, and multiple psychiatric disorders (HRs = 1.72-2.74), whereas chronic airway disease was significant only in mood disorders. Cardiometabolic and musculoskeletal conditions were not associated with mortality after adjustment. Different multimorbidity categories are associated with increased mortality among adults with cancer and PMI. These findings underscore the importance of jointly considering psychiatric and physical health comorbidities in cancer care.

items.title: Advanced In Vitro Platforms for Experimental Liver Research: From Organoids and Liver-on-Chip to Omics and Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: Hepatocytes perform essential physiological functions in the human body. Gaining more profound insight into the liver structure, diseases, and physiology by using in vitro models can help to propose more relevant clinical applications. Conventional in vitro liver models, such as two-dimensional (2D) cell cultures, fail to adequately replicate the hepatic microenvironment, even when improved by adding additional cell types and extracellular matrix (ECM). These models do not address all necessary key components to mimic in vivo conditions, particularly multicellularity, specific ECM, and proper biophysical and biochemical parameters. Organoids, 3D-bioprinted constructs, and liver-on-chip platforms establish physiologically relevant models by improving cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions and multicellular architecture. For a comprehensive understanding of the liver's interconnections with related tissues and organs, a multi-organ-on-chip is a useful platform for more systemic studies. Also, other interdisciplinary approaches, particularly omics and artificial intelligence (AI), can enhance the accuracy of experimental and pre-clinical data achieved by such advanced in vitro liver platforms. This review highlights developing platforms for integrated approaches in experimental liver studies to enable researchers to have a holistic view of the liver in physiologic and pathologic conditions.
